title: The image grading and canonical Proj morphism of a homogeneous quotient
statement: Let $R$ and $A$ be commutative rings with an $R$-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and let $\mathcal A=(A_n)_{n\geq0}$ be a nonnegative grading by $R$-submodules [def-sfb-nonnegative-graded-algebra]. Let $I\subseteq A$ be a homogeneous ideal, meaning that every homogeneous component of an element of $I$ lies in $I$. Write $q:A\to A/I$ for the quotient algebra homomorphism. Define $(A/I)_n=q(A_n)$ as an actual $R$-submodule of $A/I$. These image submodules admit a unique graded-algebra decomposition; the quotient grading is that unique decomposition. The canonical graded ring homomorphism is $q$ itself with these source and target gradings. The quotient-induced Proj morphism $\operatorname{Proj}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj] is the map of schemes induced by this graded homomorphism: on positive homogeneous standard opens its comorphism sends $a/f^e$ to $q(a)/q(f)^e$. The irrelevant-ideal condition for this Proj morphism follows from surjectivity of $q$. This includes $I=A$ and the zero quotient.
